name: Mastercard
description: Mastercard runs a global card-payments network: it does not lend or hold the cards, but charges banks (issuers), merchants' banks (acquirers) and others fees each time a card is used, on the dollar volume (assessments) and on each switched transaction. A second, faster-growing stream sells services on top of that network: security and fraud tools, data and analytics, consumer-acquisition and loyalty programmes, account-to-account payments and open-banking data. Customers get rebates and incentives that are netted out of the revenue, so the reported revenue is after what Mastercard pays banks to issue its cards. It reports a single segment and discloses two revenue categories.

employees.note: Approximately 39,800 employees (about 70 percent outside the US), plus about 6,000 contingent workers.

businessLines.name: Payment network
businessLines.how: Fees charged to issuers, acquirers and other customers as a percentage of volume and per transaction: domestic assessments on card dollar volume, cross-border assessments on volume crossing borders or currencies, and transaction-processing fees per switched transaction; net of rebates and incentives paid to customers.

businessLines.name: Value-added services and solutions
businessLines.how: Sells security and fraud-prevention, data and analytics, consumer acquisition and engagement, payment gateways, account-based payments and open-finance services to banks, merchants and governments; fees per use or per contract, growing 23 percent in FY2025 vs 12 percent for the network (computed: 13,315 vs 10,832; 19,476 vs 17,335).

brands.name: Mastercard
brands.note: Flagship network brand; GDV $10.6T in 2025, 175.5B switched transactions
